original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Prove the exact shortest unsigned word for the depth-three dirty chain connector z1 += B1 x, z2 += B2 z1, y += B3 z2 over every characteristic m >= 2 and every nonzero target residue c: 3m calls, except 4m at (m,c) = (2,1), (3,2), (4,3). Record exact depth-four minima for m = 2, 3, 4 (and m = 5 as an opt-in run).
scope_change_reason: The live handoffs assign multi-source, F3 census and signed-ring connector questions elsewhere. This self-contained side question lengthens the one-source chain by one complete call instead of increasing the source count, and asks whether the per-letter floor km survives at depth three. It does not extend a source-count census or claim a supplier improvement.
bottleneck_link: A recursive boundary that routes through two dirty intermediates pays this exact call count. The result shows when the naive per-call floor is attained and that it fails at depth four in small characteristic. No selected consumer is supplied; this is a scheduling side result, not a paid-profile or kappa gain.
stop_rule: Finish one uniform depth-three proof with exact finite exception certificates, bounded depth-four searches, literal dirty replay and source-bound publication checks; no depth-four all-m theorem or supplier construction.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the reduction to interval subword counts, the 3m floor, the explicit all-m construction and the finite exception argument. verify.py checks exact UT4(Z/m) breadth-first minima, an independent balanced-word census, every constructed word through m=256, literal noncommuting dirty replay and controls, with a generated source-hash receipt.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact depth-four minimum for every characteristic m?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The per-letter floor 4m fails for m = 2..5 (12, 18, 20, 25 calls). Whether it returns for large m decides whether deeper dirty chains pay a fixed or growing premium over one call per level per unit of characteristic.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the cut-point construction of Lemma 3 to a 1-2-3 skeleton with three slopes and test it against exact UT5(Z/m) search at m = 6 and 7.
open_questions.blocked_by: Plain breadth-first search over UT5(Z/m) has m^10 states; m >= 6 needs a quotient or meet-in-the-middle search.

open_questions.question: Can a concrete recursive caller use a depth-three chain with a favorable complete invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The call count is exact, but admission, dispatch and routing of two dirty intermediates are unpriced.
open_questions.first_step: Locate one pinned caller that composes three complete calls through dirty workspace and price all 3m calls plus its frame changes.
open_questions.blocked_by: No selected-supplier caller is bound here.
